## Painted Porch Strategies (PPS): operating context

This project is the Painted Porch Strategies website. It is Painted Porch Strategies' own space, with its own website, code, database and client
delivery. Other businesses in the portfolio have their own projects: never bring their branding,
voice or data in here.

### Client records

Every business in the portfolio is moving off GoHighLevel (GHL), the CRM in use today, to
self-managed CRM and marketing. Don't build anything new on GHL: no new pipeline, nurture,
lead-generation, or client or resource delivery features. Existing GHL writes keep running until
they are migrated. Change them only to keep them working.

New intake and lead capture from this site goes to the PPS Ops Hub, Painted Porch Strategies' own operations platform, not to GHL.

Whatever system holds client records:

- One person, one record: match on email so you never create a duplicate. An email typed into a form doesn't prove who sent it, so an unverified submission may add to an existing record but never overwrite or remove what is there.
- On every contact, keep the email, the brand ("Painted Porch Strategies"), the source (which page or form), the date, and any consent exactly as the person gave it. Brand and source are fields, never tags. A deal belongs to one brand ("Painted Porch Strategies").
- Choose pipelines and stages by ID, never by name.
- Keep CRM and API keys server-side (edge or server functions only), never in browser code.
- Never copy another business's client records into this project.

### Business decisions

A decision that concerns only Painted Porch Strategies, such as its own offers, pricing, or a tool
only PPS uses, is recorded in the PPS Ops Hub's decision register. A decision that affects another
business or the whole portfolio, such as shared tools, roles or accounts, is made in the portfolio's
internal operations hub. If a request would change one of these, flag it instead of deciding it in
code.

### Knowledge-base publication

Every Google Doc used as an Ops Hub knowledge-base view must have a substantive, committed repository source. The repository is authoritative; the Doc is a supporting visual view. Use native Google Docs, not uploaded Word or Markdown files. Keep source path, full commit, version/status and source/view links aligned. Project snapshots are dated references: check current repository main and the linked Doc before relying on a current decision. Deliver repository and native-Doc links by default, not ZIP or Word exports.

# Project rules
- Website imagery follows PPS-DEC-0023 in the PPS Ops Hub (`docs/decisions/PPS-DEC-0023-website-imagery-rules.md`): never an AI-generated face; hands or other parts of a figure with no face showing are allowed; otherwise use abstract imagery, objects and scenes; no cartoon-style images; each image on one page only. Real photos of the real team are allowed. The speaking hero, four workshop thumbnails and talk covers are existing exceptions listed in the record; don't add to them. Why: PPS Admin set these rules on 2026-11-05, restated them on 2026-11-07, and the same day narrowed the people rule to faces ("passenger to pilot only has hands, that's ok and allowed. It's just not faces"). Check every candidate image before proposing it, unused files included. Unused files showing AI-generated faces, among them portraits named after Amy, Rob and Sierra that were not them, were deleted on 2026-11-07 at PPS Admin's request.

- Buttons, form fields, cards and callout boxes have 4px corners: plain `rounded` on every link or button drawn as a button (solid fill or outline), every text field, text area, select and date picker, and every card, callout box, panel and rounded image or video frame. The shared `Button`, `Input`, `Textarea` and `SelectTrigger` carry it. Use `rounded`, not `rounded-md`, `-lg`, `-xl` or `-2xl`: the first two follow the theme's `--radius`, which differs inside and outside the new design, and the larger ones are retired. One exception: the floating header bar and its Find Your Next ShIFt button stay pills. Topic tags, filter chips, round icons and photos of people stay round. Archived and unused pages are left as they are. Why: PPS-DEC-0028; PPS Admin, 2026-11-07, first "all cta buttons ... straight with no rounded corners", then choosing a compromise between square and pill: "4px on all buttons and form fields, with the header button staying a pill? yes"; of the header, "I still like like the pill bar best"; and on 2026-11-08, revising "keep them square for now": "4px on all cards and boxes". Tests in `src/components/v3/__tests__/SiteChrome.test.tsx`.

- Button text on the public site is set in spaced capitals with the `cta-label` class (`src/styles/v3.css`: Poppins SemiBold 11px, 0.28em, uppercase), on every link or button drawn as a button, the header and footer included. The shared `Button` adds it to its solid and outline variants through `PublicSiteContext`, which `PPSLayout` provides (dialogs inherit it); ghost, link and icon buttons and staff screens are left as they are. Custom buttons carry the class themselves, and so do the link-in-bio pages (/amy, /rob, /sierra, /overview), which render outside `PPSLayout`. On a button, ShIFt reads "SHIFT" with its IF bold. Tags, chips, tabs, cards and text links keep their own type. Why: PPS-DEC-0028 in the PPS Ops Hub; PPS Admin, 2026-11-07, "I liked the spaced all caps cta buttons", then choosing "ShIFt becomes SHIFT" over keeping the wordmark's casing. It departs from the Brand Bible (6.6, 6.11, 4.5), as the record explains. Tests in `SiteChrome.test.tsx`.

- Public copy invites rather than pushes. Painted Porch is a partner and co-architect: never the one who helps, supports, assists, provides, delivers or serves (Brand Bible 4.4), and never a guide or fixer (Principle 5). Don't compare the reader, "most organizations" or "most change work" unfavourably with PPS ("Most change work starts at Take Off. Ours starts…"); say what PPS does on its own terms. Don't tell the reader what they or their organization need. Lead with Painted Porch's expertise, insight and clear point of view as advisors, so the reader is pulled to want it; never shrink that to sharing ideas or opinions. Reality checks are welcome when they follow the Architecture of Change keynote: name a real condition as information, never as the reader's failure, then turn it toward a choice. Help and support may still describe what clients, their cultures and systems, or charities do, and framework step names such as P.A.T.H. step 9 stay. Why: PPS Admin, 2026-11-08: "we don't use service language (help, support, etc)"; messaging should "position all of this as something they are pulled to do vs. think they have to do or that is a 'fix' for their problems"; "it's ok to include some reality check moments, since that's really the core message of my keynote"; and of step 9, "it's what THEY do, not us"; and of "what your organization needs", "We don't tell them what they need - we share the ideas, insights, perspective, and position for what they would be pulled to want", then of "We share ideas, insights and perspective, and you decide what you want to build", "this dimishes the value and impact of what we do. I still want to lean on our expertise and advisory". Tests in `src/test/copy-voice.test.ts` cover the new-design pages and, since the 2026-11-08 Batch 1 and Batch 2 reviews, the speaking, workshop, masterclass, Leadership Lab, resources and assessment pages, including a check that Painted Porch is never "a guide".

- Write in plain language, close to an 8th-grade reading level, following the PPS language rules and the Amy Author guidelines (plain over constructed). Plain is not generic: keep Painted Porch's own language, which carries the message: change origination, strategic authorship, architecting change, epic shIFt, extraordinary teams, becoming, and the manifesto. Change is the outcome, so don't swap these for a generic "change". "Architect" and "architecture" are core: keep them for the concept (fortifying your organizational architecture, the three Painted Porch Pillars™), the offers, "co-architect", and architecting change or your next shIFt. Replace only hollow filler ("transformation architect capacity", "the architecture your organization actually needs"), and don't default to "author" in its place. "Transformation" on its own becomes "your next shIFt" or one of the terms above. Stage four of the P.A.T.H. is Create Habits; "Habits" is fine now and then for short. Why: PPS Admin, 2026-11-08: "while 'architecture' is our word, I'd like to use it only when it reinforces the work or concepts we're describing"; "I'd like to - as a whole across the site - aim for clarity and simple language (based on pp language and amy author guidelines). This should be close to 8th grade comprehension vs. college"; of item 10, "'transformation architecture capacity' sounds like a gobbledegook"; "architect and architecture should be preserved for when speaking about the concepts and the offers related to it ... when 'architecture' or 'architect' is used more generally, it gets lost in the message"; then "I'm worried that by simplifying the language we're losing what makes us unique in our messaging ... we're really about change origination, strategic authorship, developing extraordinary teams who can do epic shift. This is about BECOMING and our manifesto", and "we've overcorrected from architect to author. I dont want to lose the plot and core messaging of what we do and what our writing and keynotes touch on"; "The 4th stage is technically Create Habits"; and later, "We can lean more on Create Habits, but you can use habits as short reference every once in a while". Short labels that would wrap and break a card row (the Embody card labels on the homepage and The P.A.T.H.) keep "Habits".

- The Epic ShIFt Organizational Appraisal is presented as the first step: it "is the basis for" Phase Zero Strategic Workshops and Architect ShIFt, or the work "begins with" or "builds on" it. Never call it "required" or "required beforehand"; "prerequisite" and "following the appraisal" are fine now and then, alongside "first step". Offers that don't build on it "stand on their own" or are "open to any team, with or without" it, rather than "not required". Why: PPS Admin, 2026-11-08: "I don't want to say 'required', instead say 'is the basis for' or 'gives insights to'", then "remove required beforehand or other versions. Phrase it in a way that notes it's the first step/precursor", and later "we can occasionally include 'prerequisite' or 'following...'". Tests in `src/test/copy-voice.test.ts`.

- The blog keeps its current template, format and copy: the Insights list (`/resources/insights`) and the post template (`PPSBlogPost`). Copy and format passes skip them (one exception: the Insights newsletter box matches the Resources newsletter line, PPS Admin, 2026-11-08), and its post links stay as they are. Why: PPS Admin, 2026-11-08: "I want to keep the blog page template/format as is."

- Pre-relaunch pages that were live are kept for reference only, hidden from visitors by page status: the old homepage (`/home-archive-v2`), Phase Zero, About, Our Approach and Our Impact (`…-archive` addresses), the two Partner With Us pages, and the nine old Ignite, Amplify and Embody pages. Don't restyle, update or delete them. Drafts and previews that were never live (three alternative homepages, four hero previews, and `/home-v2`, `/how-we-work`, `/epic-shift`, `/capabilities`) were deleted on 2026-11-08. They were never public, so their addresses now show Page not found; commit `224c3d0` (the PR #23 merge, the last before the deletion) holds them for restoring. Why: PPS Admin, 2026-11-08: "I'd like to keep the prior used pages from the website for reference only", after approving deletion of the unused ones.

- Masterclasses and mini courses: until one of them is live in `course_launch_status` (slugs starting `mc-`), `/masterclasses` and the Masterclasses option on For Individuals say "Launching soon", and a session's own landing page is linked only once that session is live (`useMasterclassLaunch`). Launching one in the admin turns this off with no code change. Why: PPS Admin, 2026-11-08: "keep the mention on the individuals page and the masterclasses page, but include a general note that they're launching soon."

- Find Your Next ShIFt, B2C results: when every program in a result's starting point is coming soon (`course_launch_status`), the guide leads with up to two live picks under "Start Here Today" and keeps the program right after it, marked "(Launching Soon)" with its launch list (`leadWithLiveStart`, picks in `START_TODAY_BY_RT` in `src/data/pathFinderQuiz.ts`). Once the program launches it leads again, with no code change. A pick shows only when its `path_finder_offerings` row is live with a link, so a new offering needs its admin row. Why: PPS Admin, 2026-11-08: "I want to offer something for B2C while these are waiting to go live", then approved this approach ("build the quiz recommendation"). Tests in `src/data/__tests__/pathFinderQuiz.startToday.test.ts`.

- Public monetary text uses native CSS text highlights from useMoneyMentions and the shared detector; never mutate React text nodes. Why: prices from static copy and asynchronous content stay consistent without changing source data or link semantics. One exception: the Phase Zero calculator's result boxes and savings line opt out with `data-money-highlight="off"`, so each figure keeps its box's color (Navy for the planned investment, Gold for the likely overrun in the AA-passing #8A5A00 from PPS-DEC-0022, Raspberry for the write-off, and the strip's blue for the savings). Why: PPS Admin, 2026-11-08: "let's make an exception for the numbers in green rule. The dollar values should match their context/boxes". Test in `src/components/pps/blue-door/__tests__/CostCalculatorDialog.test.tsx`.

- AI features and integration health checks use server-held Lovable AI credentials, never direct Anthropic credentials. Why: one gateway owns the app's AI access and obsolete provider secrets must not be required.

- LinkedIn article reading lives only in `supabase/functions/_shared/linkedin-article.ts`; the scanner imports through `import-linkedin-article` instead of parsing pages itself. Why: two copies of the cleanup rules drifted apart and broke imports.
- `youtube_videos` and `media_appearances` use `review_status` (pending/published); RLS hides pending from the public and public queries also filter on it. Why: scanned imports must wait for admin approval.
- Media appearance structured data uses the shared `src/lib/media-appearance-seo.mjs` builder in the public page and prerender pipeline, independent of filters and page SEO overrides. Why: crawlers and browsers must receive the same approved-only summaries.
- Public SELECT policies separate anonymous published-only reads from authenticated reviewer checks. Why: private role-check functions must not execute for anonymous visitors.
- Resource opt-ins queue email through `_shared/resource-email.ts` with explicit server credentials, report queued/suppressed/failed separately, and never block immediate access on email failure. Why: optional email copies must not gate resource access or silently claim delivery.
- Individual media pages use stable record IDs and the shared media SEO builder in React and prerender, with share-sized thumbnail copies generated at publish time. Why: per-appearance metadata must agree across browsers and social crawlers without requiring new editorial fields.
- Catalogue and relaunch SEO cleanups retain changed records in protected archive tables before retiring or clearing them. Why: editorial cleanup must remain reversible without exposing archived content publicly.
- Weekly content discovery uses one dedicated-secret callback for both scanners and pending-only imports; its scheduler credential table is service-role-only, and LinkedIn scheduled imports use the newsletter author's stable profile ID. Why: unattended discovery must not expose credentials or rely on an expiring browser session.
- Press kit media reads the existing media_appearances registry with both a published-only query and approval guard. Why: staff preview must not accidentally include pending imports or create a second media catalogue.
- The downloadable press kit is a dated static PDF in public/downloads, using existing page copy and published media only; refresh it when press materials change. Why: a same-origin file downloads reliably without adding browser PDF dependencies.
- Press forms share PressInquiryForm and submit-press-inquiry; the server fixes CRM destination IDs and email recipient, records consent on the opportunity, and only adds metadata to existing contacts. Why: unverified inquiries must not overwrite identity or let callers choose CRM destinations.
- Newsletter forms share useNewsletterSignup and submit-newsletter-optin; the server matches contacts by email, appends metadata, and preserves DND without opportunity writes or an email handoff. Why: subscriber capture stays separate from work inquiries and cannot overwrite existing identity and consent preferences.
- Work inquiry endpoints queue requester receipts through `_shared/inquiry-email.ts` after CRM save, using the shared contact-confirmation template and event-based idempotency; pages do not send their own copies. Why: closing a page must not interrupt receipt handoff or create duplicate emails.
